name: Any2Full
plain: Any2Full: metric depth completion that prompts Depth Anything V2 with a sparse depth map of any pattern and density, in small, base and large. Apache-2.0 code and weights.
summary: Any2Full (2026): one-stage depth completion that prompts Depth Anything V2 with a sparse depth map of any pattern and density; the depth tokens modulate the ViT features entering the DPT head, the disparity is fitted to the prompt.

papers.title: Any to Full: Prompting Depth Anything for Depth Completion in One Stage

limitations: The depth map is required: call the model with `prompt_depth=` a metric map in metres (any size, sparse points or holes as 0 / NaN / inf). The output is fitted to it by scale and shift in disparity, so it needs at least two distinct valid values.
Export has a fixed input size.
task_io: Input: one RGB image. Output: a depth or inverse-depth map. `kind` (a card field, `result.kind`) says what the numbers mean: `metric` = metres; `scale_invariant`, `affine_invariant`, `affine_invariant_log` (log depth) and `affine_invariant_inverse` are relative (unknown scale or shift, not metres). Metric models that use the focal length take `model(image, intrinsics=K)` (K `[3, 3]`, pixels of the input): `metric3d-vit-large` and `da3metric-large` need it for correct metres (`da3metric-large`: metres = output x focal / 300; without `intrinsics=` a 300 px focal length is assumed, wrong for a real camera). `unidepth-v2-vitl14`, `unik3d-vitl`, `depth-pro` and MoGe estimate the camera themselves (given `intrinsics=` replace `fx`); `zoedepth-nk` and the relative models (`da3mono-large` too) take none. Normals-only models (`kind` `none`) return `result.normals` `[B, H, W, 3]` (unit vectors, camera frame: x right, y down, z forward).

quality.title: NYUv2 test (every 4th: 164 images) with a 192x256 depth prompt, AbsRel / delta1 (metric)
quality.protocol: AbsRel / delta1 after a least-squares scale + shift fit (in disparity space for inverse-depth models), mean over images. Prompt depth models: the prompt is a 192x256 low-resolution depth built from the ground truth (mean of the valid pixels per cell, holes filled with the nearest cell), the output is metric depth compared without any scale fit; AbsRel / delta1 over the pixels with ground truth, mean over images. The prompt comes from the ground truth, so the numbers are not comparable with the paper's (ARKitScenes / ScanNet++ with a LiDAR prompt, L1 in mm): they compare our modes with the original.

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.005 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 1.5 % and p99 <= 5 % of the reference's median |value| (absolute error of the output `depth`).
